kill: KILLED on a corpus where ALL FOUR AXES DENOTE, which closes run 1's scope limitation. On the primary target the four-axis encoding reached macro_f1 0.3463 at 278 bits and lost to every required comparator: NATIVE 0.7241, LEARNED_NO_PLACEMENT 0.5556, ALTERNATE_TWO_AXIS 0.4873 at 91 bits, ONE_AXIS 0.4537 at 43 bits. Axelrod's own two 1984 descriptors — nice x provocable — beat the proposal at ONE THIRD its code length. On is_nice, four comparators scored a perfect 1.0000 while the proposal scored 0.4296 against a 0.4286 baseline. The 0.8 floor was reached on no target. §4's decision rule requires beating NATIVE, ONE_AXIS, ALTERNATE_TWO_AXIS and LEARNED_NO_PLACEMENT; on the primary target it beat none.
survivor: Two findings favour the encoding and are recorded rather than buried. (1) Unlike run 1, it is NOT at the majority baseline: 0.3463 against 0.1818 on the primary target, and 0.4845 against 0.3962 on nash_vs_self. It carries real signal — it is dominated, not empty. (2) The ADDED_AXIS kill did NOT fire: adding an independently motivated fifth axis (forgiveness) produced no material gain, which is weak evidence that the four are not obviously missing a neighbour in their own terms. Per §5 the chart survives as visualization, interpretive vocabulary and hypothesis generator. SCOPE: two corpora now, both complete enumerations, one comparator class, one learner. Axis 4's reading of self-conditioning as 'represented power' is a declared INTERPRETATION and the most contestable choice in this run.
